title: Why Talking to AI Isn't Always Enough
subtitle: Normal words for ideas, JSON for precise control.
intro: Same idea in Veo 3 — a model in a long shaggy red fur coat, dark red-lit room — but one video looked exactly cinematic. The difference? How the prompt was written.
takeaway: Use natural prompts to explore ideas, and JSON prompts when you need precise, repeatable control over an AI video.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: filming a friend
sections.body:
Imagine you tell a friend "make it cool and red." They will guess. If you hand them a shot list — lighting: red, coat: long shaggy fur, cut: invisible — they follow it.

JSON prompting is that shot list for AI. JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) just means labeled boxes for each choice, so the model doesn't have to guess.

But why bother with a list instead of just talking?

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Control you can repeat
sections.body:
You use natural prompts to explore. You use JSON prompts to control.

In Google Veo 3, both made the same dark red fashion scene, but the JSON version let the creator set style, lighting, and invisible cuts as separate dials instead of one dice roll.

More control feels like a superpower, but it creates a new problem.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When precision traps you
sections.body:
What fails if you over-control? Your JSON prompt gets rigid — one small change breaks the look and is hard to fix.

You can also waste hours tweaking fields for a seamless transition that a simple sentence could have made.

So explore with natural language first, then switch to JSON only when you need that exact look.

nodes.label: Natural prompt: 'make it red and cinematic'
JSON prompt: {lighting: red, coat: fur, cut: invisible}

steps.narration: You want a dark red fashion video.
A natural prompt leaves choices to the model to guess.
A JSON prompt labels each choice so nothing is guessed.
Veo 3 reads either and generates the scene.
Natural gives variety, JSON gives repeatable control.

quiz.q: What is a JSON prompt in this context?
options: A labeled shot list for the AI, with separate fields for lighting, style, and cuts
A longer natural sentence with more adjectives
A video file that Veo 3 copies
A filter you add after the video is made
quiz.why: The save shows JSON prompting as structured control over cinematic style, lighting, and cuts vs a normal sentence.

quiz.q: When should you prefer JSON over a natural prompt?
options: Always, because it is more professional
When you need precise, repeatable control over the look
When you want the AI to be more creative
When you have no idea what you want
quiz.why: JSON trades exploration for control — useful when you know the exact look you need.

quiz.q: What can go wrong if you use a huge JSON prompt for everything?
options: The video will render faster no matter the prompt
It can become rigid, hard to fix, and waste time when a simple sentence would work
Google Veo 3 will refuse natural prompts forever
Your JSON will automatically improve the model's quality
quiz.why: Over-specifying makes prompts brittle and time-consuming — precision is not always needed.
